aspects.says: A single item over the budget must be a leaf, and the split point must stay strictly inside the range, or the task splits into itself until the stack overflows.
basis: section:When You Know What Each Item Costs, Split by Cost

aspects.says: Chunks known in advance can be forked from a loop, as invokeAll does, keeping the stack one level deep.
basis: section:The Split Point Sets the Depth: Halve, or Fork the Chunks From a Loop
aspects.reason: invokeAll is practised in unit 6.6.1.3; here the point is the stack depth, which the quiz checks through the peeling question

aspects.says: A started leaf is never shared, so uneven work needs leaves small enough that the costly items spread over many of them; one or four leaves per worker leave workers idle.
basis: section:Uneven Work Needs Many More Leaves Than Workers

aspects.says: Forking one chunk and computing the rest recursively adds a stack frame per chunk and overflows on large inputs; halving adds a level per halving.
basis: section:The Split Point Sets the Depth: Halve, or Fork the Chunks From a Loop

aspects.says: Work-stealing moves only queued tasks; neither stealing nor more workers shares a leaf that has started.
basis: section:Uneven Work Needs Many More Leaves Than Workers

aspects.says: The number of leaves is sized from the parallelism of the pool the task runs in, not from the machine's processor count.
basis: section:Uneven Work Needs Many More Leaves Than Workers

aspects.says: When item costs are known, a threshold in cost and a split point at half the cost balance the work with few tasks.
basis: section:When You Know What Each Item Costs, Split by Cost

aspects.says: How much faster a split runs is visible only as time, which varies by machine and load.
basis: section:Uneven Work Needs Many More Leaves Than Workers
section:The Split Point Sets the Depth: Halve, or Fork the Chunks From a Loop
aspects.reason: a graded test cannot assert on timings or steal counts; the practices check the structure that produces the speed (pieces per worker, cuts by bytes) instead

aspects.says: On even work an uneven split ratio makes a deeper tree and more tasks but no slower a job.
basis: section:The Split Point Sets the Depth: Halve, or Fork the Chunks From a Loop
